intent: P7 Sprint 2 batch: 6 alembic migrations (T0 CONFIG + T1/T2/T3 utility sub-types + T4 ALTER util_results + T5 summary) + 4 nullable Float fields + CHECK constraints + 1 seed script.
scope_tier: primary: lines in pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_open_009_*.py + util_results ALTER + scripts/p7_open_009_t0_seed_energy_conversion_factors.py + openapi.json/openapi-baseline.json drift check

summary.overall_assessment: All 6 migrations + 1 ALTER are mechanically correct DDL (UUID PKs, FK ondelete CASCADE/SET NULL consistent across all 5 new tables, CHECK ranges bounded correctly, enum column lengths fit values, no NOT NULL-without-backfill hazards since all 4 T4 ALTER fields are nullable Float). Migration chain integrity verified: p7_s1_005 → p7_s1_002 → T0 → T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5. Index model↔migration parity confirmed. Two P1 issues require human attention: (1) 4 new util_results columns not exposed in UtilResultsResponse (likely intentional aggregator-output pattern but undocumented in spec diff); (2) seed script runs OUT-OF-BAND of alembic and there is no post-deploy SQL guard in the migration to assert config_energy_conversion_factors has 6 rows.

findings.title: SCHEMA DRIFT: 4 new util_results columns missing from UtilResultsResponse in openapi.json + openapi-baseline.json
evidence: pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_open_009_004_auxiliary_consumption_4fields.py:39-74 ADD COLUMN electrical_power_kwh_yr / fuel_gas_consumption_nm3_yr / steam_consumption_t_yr / cooling_water_consumption_t_yr to util_results

docs/openapi.json UtilResultsResponse properties (sampled): ['util_result_id','project_id','workspace_id','business_date','consumption_json','jsonb_deprecated','source','created_at','updated_at'] — 4 new fields NOT present
docs/openapi-baseline.json UtilResultsResponse identical to openapi.json (md5 b7577023... both files) — baseline also missing 4 fields
app/models/util.py:87-106 declares all 4 fields with nullable=True matching migration, so model↔DB is aligned but API contract lags
findings.rationale: T4 ALTER adds 4 columns to util_results (auxiliary_consumption aggregator outputs). UtilResultsResponse Pydantic schema in app/schemas/util.py did NOT add corresponding fields, so the regenerated openapi.json does not surface them. This may be intentional (callers consume them via utility_energy_summary endpoints per D1 裁决 1A '5 表权威 + JSONB deprecated'), but the migration docstring claims '聚合 T1/T2/T3 子表 annual_consumption' (aggregation results stored in util_results), implying the values ARE queryable via util_results. If a frontend or external consumer reads UtilResultsResponse expecting these fields, they will silently get undefined. No util_results API endpoint surfaces them.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) extend UtilResultsResponse + UtilResultsCreateRequest with the 4 nullable fields in a follow-up Sprint 2.x patch (manual, gated by review of frontend consumers), or (b) document explicitly in P7-OPEN-009 §3.2.2 that util_results.electrical_power_kwh_yr et al. are write-only aggregator outputs consumed only via the utility_energy_summary API. Add docstring comment in app/models/util.py:87 pointing to consumer endpoint.
findings.post_deploy_verification: SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='util_results' AND column_name IN ('electrical_power_kwh_yr','fuel_gas_consumption_nm3_yr','steam_consumption_t_yr','cooling_water_consumption_t_yr'); — expect 4 rows.

findings.title: OUT-OF-BAND seed script: config_energy_conversion_factors seed not enforced by migration
evidence: pcs-backend/scripts/p7_open_009_t0_seed_energy_conversion_factors.py:140-167 main() runs DELETE+INSERT outside alembic chain
pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_open_009_t0_config_energy_conversion_factors.py:35-88 upgrade() only creates the table, no data insert

pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:154-159 _compute_totals uses hardcoded fallback (0.1229/0.4040 for ELECTRICITY, 1.0/1.4286 for FUEL_GAS, etc.) when DB rows missing — masks deploy order bug
findings.rationale: T0 migration creates config_energy_conversion_factors table but does NOT seed 6 rows. Seeding is a separate script invoked manually (`uv run python scripts/p7_open_009_t0_seed_energy_conversion_factors.py`). Deployer may forget, leading to empty config table. Service fallback hardcodes the same factor values, so summarize_energy_year will appear to work but produce values derived from code-embedded constants rather than GB/T 50441-confirmed coefficients — defeating the CONFIG-table audit trail. Process note in the script: '工艺室 2026-10-15 签署后填 confirmed_by/confirmed_at' — until then all 6 rows have NULL confirmed_by/confirmed_at.
findings.recommendation: Add a follow-up migration `p7_open_009_t0b_seed_energy_conversion_factors` that does an INSERT...ON CONFLICT (energy_type) DO NOTHING for the 6 SYNTHETIC_TEST_DATA rows, so the deploy is reproducible from `alembic upgrade head` alone. Alternative: keep separate script but add a post-deploy SQL assertion (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM config_energy_conversion_factors WHERE source='SYNTHETIC_TEST_DATA'`) to deploy runbook + alert on != 6.
findings.post_deploy_verification: SELECT energy_type, toe_factor, standard_coal_factor, source, confirmed_by, confirmed_at FROM config_energy_conversion_factors ORDER BY energy_type; — expect exactly 6 rows; confirm_by/at may all be NULL until 工艺室 2026-10-15 签字.

findings.title: CHECK constraint addition on util_results (T4) requires full table scan + ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
evidence: pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_open_009_004_auxiliary_consumption_4fields.py:75-97 op.create_check_constraint for 4 ck_util_results_*_non_negative without NOT VALID clause
PostgreSQL op.create_check_constraint defaults to VALIDATE which scans the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCK
findings.rationale: On a production util_results table with N rows (typically <10k for an early-stage system, but could grow), the 4 CREATE CHECK constraints take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCK during validation. Existing rows have NULL for the 4 new columns (nullable=True, no DEFAULT), so they pass validation trivially, but the lock duration is proportional to row count. For util_results with millions of rows (post-Sprint 3 scaling), this is a 5-30s blocking window per constraint = up to 2 minutes total. Could use `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK (...) NOT VALID` followed by `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` later (takes ShareUpdateExclusiveLock, non-blocking).
findings.recommendation: For now acceptable (util_results is small). For Sprint 3+ when row count grows, refactor T4 to use NOT VALID + manual VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate migration. Document expected deploy window in P7-OPEN-009 release notes.
findings.post_deploy_verification: SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='util_results'::regclass AND contype='c'; — expect 4 ck_util_results_*_non_negative constraints.

findings.title: T4 ALTER util_results.electrical_power_kwh_yr et al. silently insert NULL on existing rows — no backfill despite P7-OPEN-009 §6.3 spec
evidence: pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_open_009_004_auxiliary_consumption_4fields.py:39-74 ADD COLUMN ... nullable=True (no DEFAULT) for all 4 fields
p7_open_009_004 docstring: '字段 nullable=True 起步（backward compat：Sprint 1 存量数据无值）；service 层 fallback 到 consumption_json JSONB 取值 (D1 裁决 1A)'
pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py does not backfill util_results.electrical_power_kwh_yr from consumption_json — it queries T1/T2/T3 subtables directly
findings.rationale: Sprint 1 data in util_results.consumption_json already contains 13-category flat dict with electricity_kwh / fuel_gas_nm3 / steam_t etc. T4 added 4 dedicated columns but did NOT backfill from consumption_json. Post-deploy, summary APIs will read T1/T2/T3 subtables (which are empty for Sprint 1 projects) and return total_toe=0 / total_standard_coal_kg=0 — silently diverging from the consumption_json ground truth. D1 裁决 1A explicitly chose '5 表权威 + JSONB deprecated' so this divergence is intentional for new records, but historical util_results rows lose their pre-Sprint-2 numbers unless backfilled.
findings.recommendation: If Sprint 1 projects have historical consumption_json data that should be preserved, add a separate backfill migration `p7_open_009_004b_backfill_auxiliary_from_jsonb` that reads util_results.consumption_json → util_results.electrical_power_kwh_yr etc. for rows where the new columns are NULL. Otherwise accept the divergence and document that pre-Sprint-2 projects must re-enter data via new T1/T2/T3 endpoints.
findings.post_deploy_verification: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(electrical_power_kwh_yr) AS with_electrical FROM util_results; — if total > with_electrical, pre-Sprint-2 rows are NULL and backfill decision applies.

findings.title: Migration chain relies on T0 seed run — no migration guards against re-run failures
findings.rationale: If alembic upgrade head fails partway (e.g., timeout mid-T3), re-running will raise `relation already exists` errors. Modern alembic supports `op.create_table(..., if_not_exists=True)` for idempotency. Recovery from partial apply requires manual `DROP TABLE ... CASCADE` + re-upgrade. This is standard alembic behavior and not a bug per se, but the migration docstring does not document the recovery procedure.
findings.recommendation: Add a rollback section to P7-OPEN-009 §6 deploy runbook: if alembic upgrade fails partway, run `alembic downgrade -1` (reverses one migration at a time) before re-attempting. For automated CI, wrap alembic upgrade in a retry that detects `DuplicateTable` and treats it as already-applied.
findings.post_deploy_verification: SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version; — expect p7_open_009_005_utility_energy_summary. SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND tablename IN ('config_energy_conversion_factors','utility_power_items','utility_fuel_gas','utility_heat_exchange','utility_energy_summary'); — expect 5 rows.

findings.title: Hardcoded unit conversion constants in service bypass config table — drift risk
evidence: service file line 154-159 uses hardcoded fallback factor dict for ENERGY when DB rows missing
findings.rationale: Service hardcodes (1) unit conversion to MJ canonical and (2) fallback factor values when DB rows missing. These constants should live in CONFIG tables per the project's P6-5+ CONFIG pattern (compound_* tables + 5-min TTL cache). Current implementation works but creates two sources of truth (hardcoded code vs config_energy_conversion_factors DB). Future engineering changes will diverge unless migrated.
findings.recommendation: File as OPEN-P7-S2-FOLLOWUP: add `unit_conversion_factors` CONFIG table in P7-6B with same 5-min TTL cache pattern. Service then reads both config_energy_conversion_factors AND unit_conversion_factors from DB.

findings.title: downgrade() index drop order is non-symmetric for utility_heat_exchange
evidence: pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_open_009_003_utility_heat_exchange.py:184-198 downgrade drops ix_utility_heat_exchange_temperature_class → ix_utility_heat_exchange_workspace → ix_utility_heat_exchange_project (reverse of create order is project → workspace → temperature_class)
findings.rationale: Cosmetic: index drop order does not match create order. Functionally equivalent since none of the indexes are FK-dependent, but asymmetric to convention. No runtime impact.
findings.recommendation: Optional cosmetic reorder to project → workspace → temperature_class for symmetry with upgrade().

rollback_path.full_rollback:
alembic downgrade p7_open_009_004  # reverses T5
                     alembic downgrade p7_open_009_003  # reverses T4 (drops 4 columns + 4 CHECK)
                     alembic downgrade p7_open_009_002  # reverses T3
                     alembic downgrade p7_open_009_001  # reverses T2
                     alembic downgrade p7_open_009_t0_config_energy_conversion_factors  # reverses T1
                     alembic downgrade p7_s1_002  # reverses T0 (drops config_energy_conversion_factors table)
rollback_path.downgrade_completeness: verified — each migration's downgrade() reverses its upgrade() in entirety (DROP TABLE / DROP INDEX / DROP COLUMN / DROP CONSTRAINT)
rollback_path.data_loss_warning: rollback to pre-T5 drops utility_energy_summary table (loses computed summary data); rollback to pre-T0 drops config_energy_conversion_factors (loses seed data — re-runnable via script).
migration_specific_notes: T4 downgrade drops 4 ck_util_results_*_non_negative constraints then 4 columns — correct reverse order
T0 downgrade drops the whole table — no partial rollback possible (acceptable since T0 has only metadata + seed data)

locking_operations: T0~T5 CREATE TABLE — each takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new table only (non-blocking on existing tables)
T4 ALTER TABLE util_results ADD COLUMN 4 nullable Float — PostgreSQL 11+ metadata-only, near-instant
T4 CREATE 4 CHECK constraints on util_results — FULL TABLE SCAN + ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; proportional to util_results row count
deploy_window_assessment.estimated_lock_duration_seconds: 5-30s per CHECK constraint × 4 = up to 120s worst case if util_results > 1M rows; <5s expected at current scale (hundreds to low thousands of util_results rows)
deploy_window_assessment.recommendation: deploy during low-traffic window; consider NOT VALID + manual VALIDATE CONSTRAINT split in P7-6B if row count grows beyond 100k

open_questions: DM-P7S2-001: Should UtilResultsResponse expose the 4 new aggregator columns, or are they strictly write-only consumed via utility_energy_summary API?
DM-P7S2-002: When will seed script run in deploy runbook — pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, or CI step? Should it be folded into alembic as a data migration?
DM-P7S2-004: Should util_results.consumption_json be backfilled into the 4 new columns for Sprint 1 historical projects, or accept the divergence and require re-entry via T1/T2/T3 endpoints?
